title: Symphony No. 5 in B-flat major
hook: Written in the last year of the war, it was meant as a hymn to the human spirit.

painting.title: In the Blue Expanse
painting.pairingNote: Swans and a sailing ship under a vast, bright sky, painted by a Russian landscape painter; an image of the freedom and light that Prokofiev wanted his “hymn to free and happy Man” to celebrate.

facts: Prokofiev wrote the symphony in about a month in the summer of 1944, mostly at Ivanovo, a country retreat where the Union of Soviet Composers let musicians work away from the war. It was his first symphony since the Fourth of 1930, and he gave it the opus number 100.
He called it “a hymn to free and happy Man, to his mighty powers, his pure and noble spirit”, and also “a symphony on the greatness of the human soul”.

He conducted the premiere himself in Moscow on 13 January 1945. As he stood on the podium, artillery fired a salute outside for a Red Army victory, and he waited for the guns to fall silent before beginning. Soon afterwards he fell and suffered a concussion, and his health never fully recovered; it was his last appearance as a conductor.

The symphony is built on a large scale, slow–fast–slow–fast, for a big orchestra with piano, harp and plenty of percussion. Its seriousness is real, but so is Prokofiev’s old humour: the scherzo and the finale are full of wit, and the last pages turn wild.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a broad, noble opening that ends in a roar (I), a mechanical, wry scherzo (II), a lyrical lament with a dark heart (III), a cheerful finale that ends in frenzy (IV).

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: Unusually, the symphony begins slowly, and the first movement keeps a measured pace throughout. Its main theme is a calm, wide-spanning melody for flute and bassoon; a second, soaring theme follows. The music grows from these into a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement of great breadth, and it ends in a huge [[coda|coda]] that roars with tam-tam and low piano.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a calm, wide-ranging melody, first played by flute and bassoon together, in octaves.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a soaring, wandering tune over trembling strings, its metre shifting.

stops.hear: Flute and bassoon together play a calm, wide melody, with a slightly tart edge
The strings take up the melody; the orchestra grows warmer and fuller
A soaring, wandering tune over trembling strings
New ideas, more rhythmic; the music gathers to a close
The opening melody seems to start again, but the harmony takes a different turn
The themes are broken up and built into exciting, louder passages
The main theme returns at full strength, harsh and dissonant
The soaring second theme returns
The whole orchestra swells; brass blaze, the tam-tam roars and the piano rumbles in its lowest notes

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Huge, sustained final chords in B-flat major

notice: The opening is played by two instruments at once, high and low. Listen for how that thin, tart sound grows into the full orchestra.
In the coda, listen for the tam-tam (a large gong) and the low piano tremolo underneath the brass. They give the end its rumbling weight.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Herbert von Karajan recorded the symphony with the Berlin Philharmonic in the Jesus-Christus-Kirche in Berlin in September 1968. His tempos are broad, especially in the first and third movements. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 1–4, followed by Stravinsky’s *The Rite of Spring*.

movements.heading: Allegro marcato
movements.summary: A [[scherzo|scherzo]] in Prokofiev’s machine-like style. Under crisp, repeated notes in the violins, a clarinet plays a snaking, syncopated tune. In the middle the music turns into a jaunty dance in three, with snare drum and tambourine. When the opening returns it is heavier and more menacing, and it rushes to a sudden end.

mainIdeas.name: The motor
mainIdeas.description: short, crisp repeated notes in the violins.

mainIdeas.name: The clarinet tune
mainIdeas.description: a snaking, off-beat melody with a music-hall swagger.

mainIdeas.name: The trio
mainIdeas.description: a jaunty tune in triple time.

stops.hear: Crisp, repeated notes in the violins; a clarinet slips in with a snaking, off-beat tune
The tune passes around the orchestra; piano and percussion add bite
The rhythm changes to a dance in three; a jaunty clarinet over strings, snare drum and tambourine
A transition; the motor rhythm creeps back, slower and heavier
The opening music returns, now darker and more menacing

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: Faster and louder, to an abrupt close

notice: Listen to the violins at the start. They act like a machine: the same short notes, again and again.
Compare the scherzo music at the beginning and when it returns. The notes are similar; the mood is not.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: The emotional centre of the symphony. A lyrical, slightly melancholy melody unfolds over a gently rocking accompaniment in triplets. Then the music darkens into something like a funeral march and climbs to a harsh, dissonant climax. The opening melody returns, and the movement ends quietly.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: long and singing, first heard in the woodwind with the clarinet prominent, later in the strings.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: a slow tread like a funeral march.

stops.hear: A soft rocking figure in triplets begins
A lyrical, slightly sad melody in the woodwind, the clarinet to the fore
The strings take up the melody, rising high; the mood deepens
The music darkens; a slow, heavy tread like a funeral march
The march builds to a harsh, dissonant climax for the whole orchestra
The opening melody returns, softened

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Quiet, like a dirge; a clarinet’s rising broken chord closes the movement

notice: Listen for the triplet accompaniment at the start. Some listeners hear in it an echo of the rocking figure of Beethoven’s *Moonlight* Sonata.
After the climax, notice how the opening melody sounds different: the same notes, after a storm.

movements.heading: Allegro giocoso
movements.summary: “Fast and playful.” After a quiet introduction in which the cellos recall the symphony’s opening theme, the clarinet launches a cheerful main tune. It returns between contrasting episodes: a balletic idea on the flute, a broad hymn in the strings. Near the end the music speeds into a frenzy, and the last bars are given to a few solo strings ticking away, interrupted by trumpets and percussion, before a final unison B-flat.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: the opening theme of the first movement, slow and hushed, in the cellos.

mainIdeas.name: The episodes
mainIdeas.description: a light, dancing flute tune; a solemn hymn for the strings.

stops.hear: Woodwind, then the cellos, softly recall a melody from the start of the symphony
The clarinet bursts out with a cheerful, bouncing tune over busy strings
A light, dancing tune on the flute
The clarinet tune returns
The strings play a broad, solemn melody like a hymn
The bouncing tune comes back, louder and more crowded
The music speeds up and grows frantic, with crashing percussion

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: A few solo strings tick away mechanically, interrupted by trumpets and percussion; a final loud unison

notice: Listen for the first movement’s theme in the slow opening. The finale begins by looking back.
In the last minute the full orchestra drops out and only a handful of string players are left, ticking like a clock. Many listeners hear the ending as more ironic than triumphant.

threads.title: The opening theme
threads.body: The calm melody of the first bars returns at the start of the finale, linking the beginning and the end.

threads.title: Slow and fast
threads.body: Two slow movements and two fast ones alternate. The slow ones carry the symphony’s weight; the fast ones keep Prokofiev’s humour alive.

threads.title: War and peace
threads.body: Written in 1944 and first heard as the guns of victory sounded outside, the symphony is both serious and confident, with shadows in its slow movements and wildness at its close.
